search_query: Plough Great Shelford CB22 pub CAMRA Hawthorn
description: A recently renovated L-shaped village local on Great Shelford's High Street pairs sage-green panelling and cream walls with assorted furniture and framed village photographs. Hawthorn Leisure's free house pours Greene King IPA plus two rotating guest ales from the SIBA list, while a large family-friendly garden and pool table draw weekend crowds. Big-screen sport covers major fixtures, live music appears at least monthly, and pizzas and burgers supplement the bar offer. Dog-friendly and close to Shelford station, it sits a few miles south of Cambridge city centre.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1817), camra.org.uk WhatPub. One of 275 pubs bought from Greene King by Hawthorn Leisure June 2014. Facebook-only online presence; no official website in queue.

search_query: White Lion Sawston CB22 pub CAMRA coaching inn
description: Reopened in November 2022 after refurbishment, this Grade II listed former coaching inn opens from a grey-beamed main bar with three handpumps and BrewBoard keg lines. Pieminister pies and mash are served from the bar, with food vans Wednesday through Sunday, while a separate billiards room hosts meetings and functions. Behind the pub, a car park, pétanque court, covered beer garden and smoking area complete a compact village high-street destination independent of any national chain.
notes: CAMRA national WhatPub (CAM/215). Queue already has Wikidata description; this CAMRA-based copy is fuller. Website whitelionsawston.co.uk failed Firecrawl scrape.

search_query: Greyhound Sawston CB22 pub restaurant CAMRA
description: The largest of Sawston's Grade II listed High Street pubs wears its timber and exposed wood handsomely in a busy dining-led room that still keeps real ale on Adnams Broadside, Greene King IPA and Sharp's Doom Bar. Lunchtime, evening and Sunday menus drive trade, with Venture Pub Company ownership following a 2018 refurb after earlier tenant changes. A beer garden, parking and disabled access support family visits, and a new manager arrived in December 2024. Ale may not be the headline, but the beers are consistently well kept.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1821), camra.org.uk WhatPub. Reopened 3 Feb 2018 after refurb. Queue has short Wikidata description; fuller CAMRA copy provided. Site thegreyhoundsawston.co.uk failed Firecrawl.

search_query: Duke of Wellington Willingham CB24 pub CAMRA
description: Exposed beams, three open fires and scrubbed candlelit tables lend rustic warmth to this low-ceilinged Willingham village local, sold by Greene King and reopened free of tie in April 2025 after refurbishment. Bare-boarded floors and a rear car park opening onto a garden create an unpretentious drinking space pouring up to four cask ales from local breweries. Food is not currently offered, but dog-friendly garden seating, quiz nights and occasional live music keep the community returning after a brief autumn 2025 closure.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1725), camra.org.uk WhatPub. Reopened free of tie April 2025; temporary closure mid-Sep to early Dec 2025. Facebook only; no official website.

search_query: Crown and Thistle Great Chesterford CB10 pub CAMRA
description: Built in 1528 as the Chequers and extended in 1603 into a coaching inn, this freehouse guards one of Essex's earliest inglenook fireplaces and a legend that James I stopped here en route to his coronation. Today an independent operation pairs a relaxed bar with a restaurant serving authentic Thai cuisine and stone-baked pizzas, backed by real ales, wines and gins. Patio seating and a heated smoking area sit outside, dogs are welcome, and locals and the village cricket team remain loyal regulars.
notes: CAMRA North West Essex WhatPub (ENW/11303), thecrownandthistle.pub. Queue has short Wikidata description. Website thecrownandthistle.pub failed Firecrawl thin scrape.

search_query: Regal JD Wetherspoon Cambridge St Andrews Street CAMRA
description: Art-deco bones from Cambridge's 1937 Regal cinema frame one of the city's largest Wetherspoon halls, spread across two floors with a licensed rear patio when it opened in 2000. Four regular cask ales and eight to ten guests rotate through busy handpump banks, complemented by Weston's and Gwynt y Ddraig ciders and streamlined value food from morning to late night. Sport screens, board games and a Friday-Saturday DJ from ten o'clock animate the barn-like space, though weekend queues can test patience in this central landmark.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1658), jdwetherspoon.com. Duplicate Regal row in OSM (also node/13142721772 JD Wetherspoon entry in batch2). Building opened as Regal cinema 1937.
